label: TP
reason: The CodeQL report correctly identifies two vulnerabilities. First, 'java/insecure-randomness' flags the use of java.util.Random for generating session tokens (lines 80-81), which is cryptographically weak. Second, 'java/xss' flags unencoded user input from request parameters being written directly into an HTML response via PrintWriter.println (lines 89-94), allowing script injection.

evidence.note: Use of insecure java.util.Random for token generation instead of SecureRandom
Direct concatenation of user parameter 'param' and Cookie name into HTML response without encoding
